review.decision: Approve isolated browser test design before implementation
review.notes: Exploratory Chrome reproduced a second automatically placed tile intercepting the first tile's Chat control. Test real pointer actions rather than forced clicks. The server fixture stores requests locally and never contacts an active installation.

cases.description: New workbench tiles use available visible space
cases.setup: Pair isolated desktop Chromium with a synthetic server at 1280 and 1440 pixels, and at 1024 pixels with extra vertical space. Two authorized panes have distinct transcript responses.
cases.action: Open both panes from the session rail. Open each Chat with a normal pointer click, enter independent drafts, switch one tile to Terminal and back, and send one synthetic message.
cases.expected: Both panels remain visible and separate without moving the first. The 1024-pixel layout uses the room below. Chat histories and drafts stay with their own pane. The fixture receives exactly one request for the selected pane.

cases.description: The workbench restores the user's explicit saved layout
cases.setup: Use a 1440-pixel browser and seed its local workbench with a hand-positioned overlapping layout.
cases.action: Open the normal paired workspace with the saved layout, then open a third pane where horizontal space is available.
cases.expected: The two saved geometries stay exact while a third tile chooses open space. The fixture receives no message.
